reach.rationale: The app rests entirely on APIs that have been stable for two years or more; it deliberately avoids even the newly-recommended Cache Components model, so there is zero experimental or recently-stable reach.

justification.rationale: No experimental or preview APIs are used at all, so there is no gratuitous novelty to justify; the choices made are the boring, stable ones.

findings.issue: Every route opts into force-dynamic plus a hand-rolled in-memory cache, the pre-16.4 model; as of Next.js 16.4 the framework recommends Cache Components for every app (default in create-next-app, slated as the default in Next 17), so this codebase will eventually need a migration.
findings.suggestion: Track the Cache Components migration path (next upgrade tooling) as a future tech-debt item; no action needed now since the current model is fully supported with cacheComponents disabled.

findings.issue: A module-level Map on globalThis is used for runtime caching instead of the framework's caching primitives; workable but not idiomatic going forward.
findings.suggestion: When migrating to Cache Components, replace the manual store with 'use cache' / cacheLife profiles so caching follows the platform's semantics.

summary: The app uses zero experimental, preview, RC, or canary APIs — every Next.js API it touches (App Router, async params/searchParams, generateMetadata, notFound, force-dynamic, next/navigation useRouter, Link prefetch) has been stable for two years or more, and the config ships no flags at all. Data fetching and caching are hand-rolled behind a single lib/api.js module, which keeps even future framework migrations localized. The only forward-looking note is that it stays on the pre-16.4 model rather than the now-recommended Cache Components, which is a conservatism choice, not a risk.
